PoliCond: Condition-Aware Ontology-Driven LLMs for Privacy Policy Analysis

Privacy policies play a crucial role in ensuring transparency and compliance of digital services under regulations like the General Data Protection Regulation. Existing research has advances in automating privacy policy analysis by leveraging language models, tuple-based knowledge representations and ontologies (or knowledge graphs) to resolve natural language ambiguities and enhance automation, thereby improving summary generation, contradiction analysis and compliance detection. However, traditional tuple representations (i.e. 3-tuples such as (entity, action, data type)) lack contextual information and fail to distinguish data collection practices under varying scenarios, leading to limitations on downstream applications. Bert-based tuple generators are also blamed for limited accuracy and information loss. In this paper, we present PoliCond, a framework that combines condition-aware tuple representations, ontologies, large language models, and novel application rules to address these challenges. Using a public dataset for comparison, our evaluation of tuple summary reveals that PoliCond achieves an 89.8% F1-score, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches while processing each policy in an efficient 8.4 seconds. Our analysis of 175 real-world applications revealed 46 privacy policies with 69 verified contradiction risks, including 48 issues undetected by prior works, while only 111 documents (63.4%) passed all compliance checks. These findings highlight the security vulnerabilities and insufficient standardization in privacy policies, and the practical value of PoliCond.
